newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity seen higher on natgas, SW demand.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity seen higher on natgas, SW demand.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were expected to open higher Thursday on stronger natural gas futures and firm cooling demand in parts of the Southwest.
"We see gas trade up here. We'll see it (power) go higher too," said a West Coast electricity dealer.

In over-the-counter business, June California-Oregon Border (COB) futures were quoted at $14.25-14.50 a megawatt hour versus Wednesday's close at $13.99, and June Palo Verde (PV) at $19.20-19.40 against $19.15.
On ACCESS, August COB traded once at Thursday's close of $19.40.
Power futures settled mixed yesterday as Northwest and Southwest cash power prices moved in opposite direction.
Market sources said the power complex would continue to follow cash market prices and natural gas futures.
Spot power supply in the West remained tight as Bonneville Power Administration has withheld sales of electricity during morning and evening peak hours.
Moreover, Canada's B.C. Hydro pulled out of the U.S. spot market this week due to the need to reduce in-flows at its Arrow project on the Columbia River in British Columbia.
Power plant outages, higher natural gas prices, and firm air-conditioning demand in parts of the Southwest would support spot PV prices, market sources said.
About 4,000 MW of generating capacity in the Southwest are currently offline for repairs or maintenance.
NYMEX June Henry Hub natgas futures opened up 0.6 cent at $2.190 per million British thermal units.
A 550 megawatt (MW) unit at the Jim Bridger coal-fired generating complex in Wyoming was set to restart today after being shut last week for repairs.
Energy demand in the Northwest would be flat as seasonal temperatures would settle across the Northwest into next week.

Air-conditioning usage in the Southwest, especially the southeastern section, would stay firm as readings in the region would average above normal. The extreme northeastern area would be cooler than other parts of the region.
